summary: Jaluit Airport (UIT) serves Jaluit Atoll, one of the largest and most historically significant coral atolls in the Marshall Islands. Located on Jabor islet, the airport provides vital air access to a remote Pacific community that was once the administrative center of German colonial operations in the Marshall Islands. The surrounding atoll is known for World War II wrecks, pristine reefs, and traditional Marshallese culture.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Jaluit Airport?
A: Air Marshall Islands operates regular domestic flights connecting Jaluit with Majuro and other atolls in the chain, typically using small turboprop aircraft suited for short island runways.

Q: Is there a terminal building at Jaluit Airport?
A: The airport has minimal facilities typical of remote Pacific atoll airstrips, with a small terminal area and basic amenities. Travelers should expect a rustic experience.

Q: When is the best time to visit Jaluit Atoll?
A: The dry season from December to April generally offers the most pleasant weather for visiting, with calmer seas ideal for boat trips to outer reef dive sites and WWII shipwrecks.

Q: Are there accommodations near the airport?
A: Limited guesthouse-style lodging is available on Jabor islet, and visitors should arrange accommodations in advance as the atoll receives very few tourists.
transport_tips: Getting from Jaluit Airport to Jabor village is straightforward as the airstrip is located on the same islet, typically a short walk or pickup truck ride. There is no public bus service on the atoll, so arranging transport through your guesthouse or local contacts in advance is recommended. Speedboat transfers may be needed to reach outer islets for diving or exploring WWII wreck sites.
local_tip: Bring small cash denominations in USD, as card payment facilities are extremely limited on Jaluit, and tipping local boat operators or guides directly is appreciated. Also, consider packing a small gift from your home country to exchange with locals, as Marshallese hospitality traditions value reciprocal sharing.
